In other words, this
scale_x_reverse()
is not what I want.

Thanks for help,
Bjørn

messages.subject_clean: How to Annotate Tree with Data From the Constructed Tree
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am a student currently using evolutionary trees for risks analysis.

I am working on visualisation of trees and find ggtree is a great package for plotting trees. But as a newbie of both R and bioinformatics, I cannot let it work properly. What I want to get are trees containing following information.

 <http://evolution.berkeley.edu/evolibrary/images/evo/sixchars_phylo.gif>

I work with binary data (0 for absence and 1 for the presence of a character), and the headers of columns are the characters (I want to annotate as these "Vertebrae", "Bony skeleton" in the above graph), and the rows are different taxons. I use phangron to construct trees and hope to annotate the nodes (or edges) with the character(s) that made the bifurcations. It is similar to your example of “annotating tree with phangorn output”, but I cannot let it work properly.

My code is as follows:

#read file from local disk in csv format. **Currently transpose does not work, do not know why**
origin <- read.csv(file.choose(),header = TRUE, row.names = 1)

origin <- t(origin)

events <- phyDat(origin, type="USER", levels=c(0,1))

#maximum parsimony to construct a tree **From official document, working properly**
dm <-dist.hamming(events)

treeNJ <- NJ(dm)

parsimony(treeNJ, events)

treePars <- optim.parsimony(treeNJ, events)

#maximum likelihood to generate iniformation, **From https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/ggtree/inst/doc/treeAnnotation.html#annotating-tree-with-ape-bootstraping-analysis**
fit <- pml(treePars, events)

fit <- optim.pml(fit, optNni=FALSE, optBf=T, optQ=T,

                 optInv=T, optGamma=T, optEdge=TRUE,

                 optRooted=FALSE, model = "GTR")

phangorn <- phyPML(fit, type = "ml")

# plot tree **From same website, in section "annotating tree with phangorn output"**
ggtree(phangorn) + geom_text(aes(x=branch, label=AA_subs, vjust=-.5))

Apologies in advance if this is a dumb question, and all comments are appreciated!

Regards,

Speed

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to plot a tree where some of the tip labels are supposed to be bold and some are to be italic.

I have read this: https://guangchuangyu.github.io/ggtree/faq/#formatting-tip-labels but it is still a bit unclear to me.

I have thought about two ways to do it. One is:

ggtree(phyloseqobject)+  geom_tiplab(aes(label=Name), align = TRUE, linetype = 0, offset = 0.04) + geom_text2(aes(label = label, fontface = "italic", subset=node %in% Mylist))+geom_text2(aes(label=label, fontface = "bold", subset = node %in% Mylist2))

Obviously, this plots the label names twice. I could off course skip the geom_tiplab part, but I really like the alignment which is made here.

Another way could be something like:
I have not included the bold part in this one, but I assume it would just be adding another "+geom_tiplab(xxx)" afterwards?

ggtree(phyloseqobject) +  geom_tiplab(aes(subset = node %in% Mylist),label=substitute(italic(x),list(x=c(1:20)[1])), parse=T, align = TRUE, linetype = 0, offset = 0.04)

Here I get this error:

Warning: Ignoring unknown parameters: label, parse
Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (20): label, hjust

Mylist has the length 20 which is why I wrote c(1:20) (could has well been a vector with 20 labels). I do not know why this error occurs.

I think the latter option is the preferable one, in order to keep the alignment, but I need to be able to overcome the error.

Frederik

I think it is not a good idea to support aligning data on the right hand side for internal nodes as it is hard to associate the data to internal nodes for us using human eye.

You can use geom_nodepoint to add data point on nodes and encode you data value as point size or color.

#First of all, thank you so much for making this package.
#I am wondering if there is an easy way to label lots of clades at once

require(ggtree)
#v1.8.1

set.seed(1234)
tree <- rtree(n=10)

#It is easy to color different clades all at once
cls <- list(Clade_1=c("t1", "t7"),
            Clade_2=c("t5", "t2", "t4"),
            Clade_3=c("t3", "t6"),
            Clade_4=c("t8", "t9", "t10"))

tree2 <- groupOTU(tree, cls)

ggtree(tree2, layout="circular", aes(color=group))+
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), hjust=-.3)+
  geom_tiplab2()

#But is there a way to label different clades all at once?

#We can do this to automate the identification of MRCA's
clades <- data.frame(Label=c("Clade_1", "Clade_2", "Clade_3", "Clade_4") , Node=NA)

for(i in 1:length(clades$Label)){

  #Get the MRCA for these taxa and put in into the dataframe
  clades[i, "Node"] <- MRCA(tree2, tip=cls[[i]])

}

#But if we try to plot all those labels at once, we get an error
ggtree(tree2, layout="circular", aes(color=group))+
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), hjust=-.3)+
  geom_tiplab2()+
  geom_cladelabel(node=clades$Node, label=clades$Label)

##########################################################
Warning messages:

  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In df$parent == node :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
3: Computation failed in `stat_clade_text()`:
  replacement has 4 rows, data has 1
##########################################################

#The best we can do is one clade label at a time
ggtree(tree2, layout="circular", aes(color=group))+
  geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=node), hjust=-.3)+
  geom_tiplab2()+
  geom_cladelabel(node=clades$Node[1], label=clades$Label[1], offset = .25)+

  geom_cladelabel(node=clades$Node[4], label=clades$Label[4], offset = .25)

#This is very annoying for large trees with many clades. Is there a way to label all the clades in one line of code?

#And while we are talking about labeling clades, is there a way to get the angle of the clade names to behave like tip labels in geom_tiplab2() ?

#Thank you for your help
